title: Mobile library
subject: ui
summary: The mobile UI library: React Native components on the same contract as the web library; how a theme reaches a component without a cascade; what a component owns; what the platform cannot do.

axioms.text: The mobile library obeys the same law and the same table as the web library.
A mobile component reads its aspect from the theme and writes none of its own.
What the platform cannot do is stated, not worked around.

purpose.intro: This repo is a seed for many products, each with its own themes, on two platforms. One vocabulary and one table across web and mobile let a theme be authored once for both and a component be checked against the same row on both; where React Native has no cascade, the engine does at build time what the browser would do at run time.

claims.text: A mobile component is one element of that table. It has the same name as its web twin and the same axis props: `emphasis`, `status`, `scale`, `state`. Its first line says which element it is and which web component, at which version, it mirrors.
The code is not shared. The web component renders HTML and is styled by CSS; this one renders React Native views and reads its style from the native theme.

One vocabulary (`emphasis`, `status`, `scale`, `state`, from `ui/types/axes.ts`) and one law (`ui/types/elements.ts`): a mobile component's props are typed from its row. A mobile theme is a `MobileTheme`: the same primitives, families, elements and cascade as a web theme, without what only the web has, with what only a phone has.

reference.statement: One table rules both libraries: `shared/libs/ui/types/elements.ts`. Each row is an element, with its family, the platforms it exists on, and the values it takes on each axis.

reference.topic: How a theme reaches a component

snippets.code:
themes/<id>/v<n>/theme.ts          a MobileTheme, authored
        │   mobile/theme-engine     (pnpm theme:build:mobile)
        ▼
themes/<id>/v<n>/generated/<id>.native.json
        │   ThemeProvider
        ▼
useElement("button", { emphasis, status, scale, states })  →  { view, text, color, icon }

reference.statement: The web engine turns a theme into CSS and the browser resolves the cascade. React Native has no cascade, so the mobile engine emits each rule as a *fragment*, in the order the cascade applies them, and `resolve` (in `src/theme/resolve.ts`) keeps the fragments whose axes match and merges them. The colour composition (tint, background alpha, `smart-bw`) is the web stylesheet's formula, computed in JavaScript.

claims.text: `ThemeProvider` takes a native theme (the `<id>.native.json` the mobile theme engine writes) and a colour mode.
`useElement(element, axes)` returns the element's style for its axes: `{ view, text, color, icon, extras }`.
`usePart(element, part, axes)` does the same for a surface inside an element (a list's row, a switch's thumb).
`useType(level)` and `useColor(name)` read a typography level and a colour.
A component never writes a colour, a size or a spacing of its own.

reference.statement: A component is themed only by reading the theme. There is no cascade in React Native.

claims.text: **Accessibility.** Role, state, label. A component without it is not done.
**Native props.** A component wraps a React Native component and passes its props through.
**Press feedback per platform.** iOS dims (`theme.press.opacityDim`), Android ripples (`theme.press.ripple`); both come from the theme. The `active` state restyles the element on both.
**Structure.** Row or column, what goes where. Never a colour, a size or a spacing.

reference.statement: `active` (pressed), `focus`, `selected`, `disabled`, `loading` are shared with the web. `long-pressed` and `swiped` are mobile's. There is no `hover`. A component computes its states from what happens to it and also accepts `state` to force one.

reference.topic: What React Native cannot do, and what stands in

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| The web has | Mobile does |
|---|---|
| The cascade | Fragments, resolved by `useElement` |
| `:hover` | Nothing. `long-pressed` is the state for what a held press reveals |
| Inherited text colour | A component passes its text style to its own text |
| A stylesheet swapped at run time | A new `theme` or `mode` on the provider re-renders its consumers |

claims.text: Every interactive component sets its accessibility role and state, and passes the native props of the React Native component it wraps.

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| Component | Element | Web twin |
|---|---|---|
| `Button` | `control--button` | Button |
| `Card`, `CardHeader`, `CardContent`, `CardFooter` | `surface--card`, `--header`, `--content`, `--footer` | Card and its regions |
| `Badge` | `surface--badge` | Badge |
| `Avatar` | `surface--avatar` | Avatar |
| `Input` | `field--input` | Input |
| `PhoneInput` | `field--phone-input` | PhoneInput |
| `Field`, `Label` | `surface--label`, `--field-description`, `--field-message` | Label and the field wrappers |
| `ChoiceGroup` | `control-group--choice-group` with `control--toggle` | the choice group |
| `Group` | `surface--group` | a titled section |
| `EmptyState` | `surface--empty-state` | EmptyState |
| `Icon` | `shape--icon` | Icon, same semantic names, same icon set (Lucide) |
| `Text` | the typography levels, `type--<level>` | the `type--*` attribute |
| `Stepper` | a composite of `button-group`, `button`, `button-group-text` | none: mobile's own |

snippets.code:
import { ThemeProvider, Button, Card, Badge, Text } from "@libs/mobile-components";
import { Stack } from "@libs/mobile-layouts";
import theme from "<themes>/bounx-mobile/v1/generated/bounx-mobile.native.json";

<ThemeProvider theme={theme} mode="light">
  <Card>
    <Stack dir="row" align="center" justify="between" gap={12}>
      <Stack gap={4} size="fill">
        <Badge>Group session</Badge>
        <Text type="heading4">Junior Squad</Text>
      </Stack>
      <Button scale="sm">Start</Button>
    </Stack>
  </Card>
</ThemeProvider>
snippets.caption: tsx

claims.text: Concepts, contextual overrides and rules (theme levels 4 to 6) are not emitted: they need a component's ancestry at run time.
Gradients, text effects and blur are not emitted; the engine lists what it skipped in the output's `unsupported`.
